slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
Quadrilaterals form a family tree using inclusive definitions.

Parallelogram: both pairs of opposite sides parallel. Rectangle: a parallelogram with four right angles. Rhombus: a parallelogram with four equal sides. Square: both a rectangle and a rhombus. Trapezoid (inclusive): at least one pair of parallel sides. Kite: two pairs of equal consecutive sides.

So every square is a rectangle and a rhombus, and every rectangle is a parallelogram. Some books use an exclusive trapezoid (exactly one pair of parallel sides); then a parallelogram is not a trapezoid. This course uses the inclusive definition and says so whenever it matters.

slides.title: Check yourself
slides.html: Is every square a rectangle? Is every rectangle a square?
slides.reveal: Every square is a rectangle (four right angles). Not every rectangle is a square; its sides need not all be equal.
